## Repository selection

Evaluate proportionately accepted content, preservation commitment, versioning, metadata, identifiers, access controls, embargoes, restricted-data support, size limits, costs, governance, longevity, export and migration options, correction/withdrawal support, community acceptance, contacts, and terms. Possible destinations include institutional, domain, general research, controlled-access, records, approved storage, and software-specific repositories. No universal repository is prescribed.

Repository certification can be useful evidence. It is not universally required, does not guarantee indefinite access, does not replace fit assessment, and does not authorize restricted deposit. The [CoreTrustSeal Requirements 2026–2028](https://www.coretrustseal.org/why-certification/requirements/) are a repository-assessment resource, not a project conformance requirement.

## Identifiers and relationships

Record a DOI, accession number, repository record ID, SWHID, archival identifier, or institutional record number where one exists. Not every file needs a persistent identifier; the package or major research object should be identifiable at a useful level. Link project, data, software, results, communication, release, preservation package, and replacement package.

## Deposit is not verification

Record submission date, recipient, package ID/version, receipt, repository identifier, accepted/rejected files, transformations, access state, embargo, license, and deposit owner. Then verify completeness, inventory, checksums or other integrity evidence, metadata, restrictions, retrieval where permitted, identifier resolution, and landing-page accuracy. An upload is not a verified preservation outcome.

## Exit planning

For consequential deposits, record account and notice ownership, fees, export options, repository closure or terms-change response, location of a second package or manifest, and migration responsibility. The public release location is not automatically the preservation repository.
